changelog: 1.0.0 (Jellyfin 12.2 to 12.4): first version. Every HLS stream Jellyfin serves gets a real quality ladder: by default 4 lower qualities down to 700 kb/s, each produced by Jellyfin itself with the same audio track, subtitles (burned-in ones too) and playback session. The player (web, Android, Apple devices) steps down when the network weakens and back up when it recovers, loading the new quality before switching: no cut, no restart. A lower quality costs nothing until a player uses it. Measured on a real Jellyfin in Chrome with the network throttled to 1.6 Mb/s for a minute: 7 s of stalls instead of 46 s, on Jellyfin 12.2 and 12.4. Optional: remote players can get the adaptive stream instead of direct play (experimental). Settings page in English, French, German and Spanish.
description: Real adaptive bitrate for Jellyfin's HLS streams: the player changes quality with the network, without a cut.
name: Adaptive Bitrate
overview: A real quality ladder in Jellyfin's HLS streams: quality follows the network, without a cut.
